Fast-absorbing carbohydrate exposure may translate into a smaller glucose rise when recent heart rate (a proxy for ongoing physical activity) is elevated, since exercise increases glucose uptake.
The glycemic impact of the most recent meal's carbohydrate load likely depends on how long ago it was eaten, since absorption dynamics evolve over time.
The relative weight of fast-absorbing carbohydrates versus slower-absorbing fat intake should indicate how quickly glucose is likely to rise, improving residual prediction.
The expected glycemic rise from a lunch carbohydrate load may be proportionally smaller when the current glucose level is already high, reflecting saturation of absorption effects.
